clue.text: Put up rainwear in a swindle

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means its letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: macs are raincoats, short for mackintoshes

explanation.surface: Someone is being sold waterproofs as part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A con or fraud is a synonym of swindle, both nouns for a dishonest trick.

clue.text: Still managed to snuggle into quilt, when drunk

indicators.note: snuggling into something means burrowing inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a drunken arrangement is a muddled one, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy burrows under a duvet and lies motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'yet', but it is the adjective for calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and undisturbed: still as an adjective, as in a still pond, is a synonym.

clue.text: The knot sailors try to avoid

definitions.meaning: the ... knot is the classic square knot used by sailors
a ridge of rock or coral just under the sea, a hazard to ships

explanation.surface: A knot that seafarers try to steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a type of knot, and an underwater ridge of rock that endangers shipping.

clue.text: Advertise sportswear for those taking the air

parts.note: to air something is to make it public, to advertise it
a strip is a team's sports kit

explanation.surface: A sports-clothing advert aimed at people out for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the air' suggests a stroll outdoors, but here it means taking off in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip for light aircraft serves pilots and passengers going up into the sky.

clue.text: Middleman to offer new shares for sale, so not going under

indicators.note: the opening of the word Middleman tells us to take the central letter of man

parts.words: to offer new shares for sale
parts.note: floating a company means offering its shares on the stock market

explanation.surface: A broker is preparing a share issue so the business survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middleman' looks like a broker, but splits as Middle + man: the middle letter of MAN is A.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying on the surface, or solvent, is the opposite of sinking or going bust.

clue.text: Man takes court action, hoping judge will be this

parts.note: Justin is a man's name
a case is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: A man sues, hoping the judge proves fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads cryptically: a litigant hopes the judge will be 'just in case', fair in the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a precaution phrase it means as insurance; split, it describes a fair judge hearing the lawsuit.

clue.text: Head branch rental adjusted

indicators.note: letters that are adjusted are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A head office's rental charge has been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head branch' sounds like a main office of a firm, but it is a branch growing from a deer's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer's horn is branched like a tree, growing out of its head.

clue.text: Little quiet cry

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A small, hushed sob.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed tears is a synonym of cry as a verb.

clue.text: Number feel concern about cut

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to care is to feel concern
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Many people are worried about a reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice or sculpt with a knife is a synonym of cut, as a verb.

clue.text: Clout, say

definitions.meaning: power or weight to sway others
having a say means having some sway over a decision

explanation.surface: Clout, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean power to affect outcomes: political clout, and a say in what happens.

clue.text: Public declaration in the show ring

parts.note: to manifest is to show or display
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An announcement made in a show ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A party publishes its policies in a published statement of aims, a public declaration.

clue.text: Switch lit up bulb

indicators.note: to switch things is to swap them round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flicking a switch lights up a light bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulb' looks like a light bulb but is a flower bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring flower grown from a bulb, so the bulb stands for the plant.

clue.text: One who throws out a bad cheque

definitions.meaning: a doorman who ejects troublemakers from a club
a cheque that is returned unpaid is said to bounce

explanation.surface: Someone rejecting a worthless cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a club doorman who ejects people, and slang for a cheque that is returned unpaid.

clue.text: Meat company included in embargo

indicators.note: one piece is put within the other

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: A meat firm has been caught up in a trade ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork from a pig's back or sides is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Firm taken in by swindles gets the police

indicators.note: being taken in puts one piece inside another, as well as hinting at being fooled

parts.note: cons are swindles
stable means firm or steady

explanation.surface: A company duped by fraudsters calls in the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective, steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers of the lowest rank, collectively standing for the police.

clue.text: A bad-tempered pet

parts.note: pet is an old word for a fit of sulking, so a bad-tempered one is an outburst, not a grumpy animal

explanation.surface: A snappy, ill-humoured cat or dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the sense of a fit of pique; an angry one is a childish fit of rage.

clue.text: Names changed to accommodate the minister

indicators.note: changed letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Names are altered to make room for a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' suggests a politician, but here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A house provided for a Presbyterian or other church minister to live in.

clue.text: Stop, or pass on

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark, a kind of stop
the large intestine, which passes waste onward

explanation.surface: Halt, or let something go by.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark of two dots, and the part of the bowel that moves digested matter along.

clue.text: Pea jacket?

parts.note: a pea jacket is a sailor's coat, but read literally it is the casing a pea grows in

explanation.surface: A sailor's short woollen coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed case of a pea plant, which wraps the peas like a coat.

clue.text: Not the best situation for a county team

parts.note: Down is a county in Northern Ireland
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A county team finds itself in a poor position.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback or disadvantage is a less than ideal state of affairs.

clue.text: Tree in a small enclosure

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A tree growing inside a little fenced plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of poplar with fluttering leaves, a common tree.

clue.text: Sad passage — quote coming up

parts.note: a path is a passage

indicators.note: in a down clue, something coming up is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A mournful passage of text, with a quotation to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful or woeful: sad in the sense of feeble or deplorable.

clue.text: Writes down memoranda at the centre

indicators.note: at the centre tells us the word at sits in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: memoranda are notes

explanation.surface: Someone jotting down reminders at the main office.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down in writing or musical notation; a synonym of records on paper.

clue.text: Teases the non-male members of the family

indicators.note: non-male means without the male, so those letters are removed

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
aunts are female relatives

explanation.surface: Mocking the women of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-male' takes HE out of THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers or gibes; to tease is a milder synonym of to mock.

clue.text: Cycle chain?

definitions.meaning: a run of works such as a song cycle or set of programmes
a chain of events in sequence

explanation.surface: A bicycle chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one sequence: a cycle of programmes or works, and a chain of linked events.

clue.text: Wind resulting from unsettled weather

indicators.note: unsettled letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gale arising from stormy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a breeze but is the verb, to twist around.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine or coil around something, a verb sense of wind.

clue.text: One of two up for approval

definitions.text: One of two up for approval

parts.words: One of two up for approval
parts.note: giving two digits pointing upwards is a sign of approval

explanation.surface: One of a pair of proposals put forward for sign-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both digits raised is a gesture of approval, so this is one of them.

clue.text: It's on course to work for the better

definitions.text: It's on course to work for the better

parts.words: It's on course to work for the better
parts.note: on a racecourse, this betting system serves the person placing a bet, the better

explanation.surface: Something that is improving steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator, the pool-betting system found at racecourses, which handles punters' wagers.

clue.text: Current increase in rent — and it's rising again

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a surge is a sudden increase in electric current

explanation.surface: Rents are going up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviving or making a comeback; resurgence is a return to strength.

clue.text: It's a swindle to put a penny on farm butter

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a piece on another places it beneath
this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter on the farm
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Charging an extra penny for farmhouse butter is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest scheme or racket; in British slang this word means a con.

clue.text: Some seem quite empty, or just the opposite

indicators.note: some of the words means just part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: Some look completely vacant, or else crammed full.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of empty is to be full to overflowing, to abound or swarm.

clue.text: It will prove ownership of river in named setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds a jewel, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: titled means named
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Documents establishing who owns a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document that establishes the right to a property.

clue.text: Major eastern state

parts.note: main means major or principal

explanation.surface: A big state in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A New England state of the USA, in the far north-east.
